title: Tusshar Kapoor Questions Cost of Mega Ensemble Films, Praises Ahmed Khan's Vision for Welcome to the Jungle
excerpt: The actor recalls being stunned by 50 vanity vans on set and wondering if the massive expenditure was justified, but credits the director's unwavering commitment to the franchise's unprecedented scale.
body:
• Tusshar Kapoor revealed that Welcome to the Jungle required nearly 50 vanity vans and 250 cars daily to accommodate its 34-actor cast.
  • The actor admitted wondering if the massive expenditure was justified but praised director Ahmed Khan for sticking to his vision.
  • Welcome to the Jungle has grossed over ₹186 crore worldwide since its June 26 release.
  • Tusshar also confirmed that Golmaal 5 is 80-90% complete and entering its final shooting schedule.

Actor Tusshar Kapoor has opened up about the staggering logistics behind Welcome to the Jungle, the third instalment of the Welcome franchise that hit theatres on June 26 with a cast of 34 Bollywood actors. Speaking to Screen, Kapoor recalled his initial disbelief at the sheer scale of the production — and candidly questioned whether it was all worth the expenditure.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=R704yP3dlXw

'Is It Really Justified?'

Director Ahmed Khan recently revealed that the film's set required nearly 50 vanity vans and around 250 cars every day to accommodate the massive ensemble. Tusshar said it often took him five minutes just to walk to his own vanity van because of the long line of parked vehicles.

https://x.com/CNNnews18/status/2080290879726911715

"I used to just look at these vans and wonder what would be the daily cost for so many vans, and everyone's staff. Is it really worth taking so many actors? But is it really justified having so many actors and doing so much kharcha?"

— Tusshar Kapoor

Despite his initial doubts, Tusshar credited Ahmed Khan's unwavering commitment to the project. He noted that the director never compromised on his vision even after a one-year gap in the shooting schedule. "Ahmed was adamant that he needed everybody in every shot. When the film resumed, he never thought to just shoot with actors available on set. He stuck to his guns and finished the film," Tusshar said, according to Bollywood Hungama.

Box Office Vindication

The gamble on scale appears to have paid off. Welcome to the Jungle, directed by Ahmed Khan and produced by Firoz Nadiadwala, has grossed over ₹186 crore worldwide against a reported budget of ₹125 crore. The film features Akshay Kumar, Suniel Shetty, Paresh Rawal, Arshad Warsi, Disha Patani, Jacqueline Fernandez, Raveena Tandon, Lara Dutta, Jackie Shroff, Shreyas Talpade, Rajpal Yadav, Johnny Lever, Krushna Abhishek, and Kiku Sharda among its sprawling cast.

Tusshar had earlier praised Ahmed Khan's approach to managing the large ensemble, telling Zoom that the director "has justified the cast in the story," calling it unprecedented in Bollywood comedy. He also lauded co-star Akshay Kumar's professionalism. "Akshay is sharp and the entire script is at the tip of his fingers. Even though he's always joking around and playing pranks, he works equally hard," he said.

Golmaal 5 Nears Completion

Tusshar is simultaneously involved in another major ensemble project — Golmaal 5, the fifth instalment of Rohit Shetty's hit comedy franchise. In an exclusive interview with Bollywood Hungama, the actor confirmed that 80-90 percent of the shoot is complete and the film is entering its final schedule.

The franchise has expanded its cast for this instalment, with Akshay Kumar joining the returning core of Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Shreyas Talpade, and Kunal Kemmu. Sharman Joshi, who appeared in the original 2006 film, is also making his return. National Award-winning actress Priyamani has joined the cast in a negative role, according to Variety India.

"Rohit Shetty is the hardest-working director I've ever worked with. He inspires me and all of us," Tusshar said. "The work I have done with Akshay sir in Golmaal 5 will be the icing on the cake for my career as well."

The Golmaal franchise has grossed over ₹600 crore across its four films. Golmaal 5 is expected to release in 2027.
